key_insight: CareMirror reframes dementia care to include caregiver wellbeing as a core part of the care ecosystem, not an afterthought. It links caregiver reflection, personalized support, and clinician sharing so caregivers can get help while staying in control of their data.
problem_solved: Family caregivers of people living with dementia often carry heavy emotional and practical burdens, but their own wellbeing is rarely monitored or supported within clinical care workflows.
method: Built CareMirror, an envisioned ecosystem with caregiver-facing and clinician-facing interfaces.
Enabled longitudinal reflection on caregiver wellbeing and personalized support over time.
Used CareMirror as a design probe in semi-structured interviews with 14 caregivers to explore needs and preferences, including caregiver-controlled sharing with clinicians.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this paper highlights how human-centered systems can support vulnerable care networks by combining personalization, longitudinal sensing/reflection, and privacy-preserving data sharing. It also shows that model-driven tools in healthcare should support both patient and caregiver outcomes.
visual_elements: Two-panel ecosystem diagram showing caregiver and clinician interfaces connected by a shared wellbeing loop
Timeline chart of caregiver reflections and support recommendations over time
Icon-based workflow illustrating caregiver-controlled sharing and privacy choices
Quote bubbles or persona cards summarizing caregiver interview themes
paper_title: CareMirror: Bringing Caregiver Wellbeing into the Dementia Care Ecosystem
paper_authors: Jiayue Melissa Shi, Ethan Nguyen, Drishti Goel, Upasana Natarajan, Shashwat Srivatsa
